chunks: Zayd al-Shahham narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
He was asked about a man who fears the absconding of his slave, or that the slave had already absconded: should he shackle him or place a mark on his neck?
He said: "He is only in the position of a camel whose bolting is feared. So if you fear that, then secure him well, feed him fully, and clothe him."
I said: "And how much is his fill?" He said: "As for us, we provide our dependents with two mudd of dates."

key_terms.أَشْبِعْهُ: feed him until he is satiated
key_terms.إِبَاقَ: absconding or running away from one's master
key_terms.رَايَةً: a distinguishing mark or sign placed on him
key_terms.فَاسْتَوْثِقْ: take firm precaution and secure him properly
key_terms.مُدَّيْنِ: two mudd, a measure of food

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about restraining an absconding slave and the duty to feed and clothe him?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on dealing with a slave feared to abscond, permitting precautionary restraint while also emphasizing the owner's duty to provide adequate food and clothing. It combines a practical legal ruling with an ethical insistence on proper maintenance of dependents.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3536 - Zayd al-Shahham narrated from Abu Abdullah (as):
He was asked about a man who fears that his slave might run away or that the slave had already run away. Should he restrain him or place a mark on his neck?
Imam (as) replied: "He is like a camel you fear might escape. If you fear that, secure him properly, feed him well, and clothe him."

I asked: "How much is sufficient to fill his hunger?"
Imam (as) said: "As for us, we provide our dependents with two measures (mudd) of dates."
